site.name: lattice
site.summary: lattice-clone Fictional hosted columnar / relational database "Lattice DB" marketing site, centered on the two-dimensional matrix on the pricing page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: technical paragraph + SQL code example + 3 features + CTA | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 6 rows (seats) × 6 columns (data volume) two-dimensional matrix; clicking a cell highlights the row and column and updates the right-side sticky quote card (with a "How this is calculated" expansion); 9 add-on checkboxes (percentage or flat add-on); bottom final monthly-fee breakdown card; 4-tier explainer (clicking a cell auto-highlights the corresponding tier); 15-row feature comparison; 8-question FAQ; footer | | `styles.css` | Brand color #6D28D9 purple; IBM Plex Sans + Mono; responsive |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full lattice system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The pricing flow is largely functional: matrix selections stay synchronized with the sticky quote card, and add-ons recalculate the estimate correctly. However, the page has clear mobile usability issues, including horizontal overflow and very small tap targets, which make key pricing controls harder to use on touch devices. Several secondary links also behave like placeholders with no meaningful destination or feedback, which weakens trust and navigation clarity. Coverage is strong on the main pricing matrix, but some adjacent controls and destinations remain only partially exercised.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively validate the Lattice DB marketing and pricing experience, with emphasis on the interactive pricing matrix, add-on pricing logic, tier explainer, feature comparison, FAQ, and mobile usability.
exploration_plan.summary: Start on the landing page to verify the primary navigation and pricing CTA, then move to the pricing page for the core matrix flow. On pricing, systematically exercise cell selection, row/column highlighting, sticky quote updates, the calculation expander, add-on checkboxes, tier explainer, and the downstream price breakdown. Finish by checking adjacent informational sections and repeating the critical pricing interactions in a mobile viewport, with special attention to the small-tap-target warnings seen in prescan.
assumptions: The site consists of only two HTML pages: index.html and pricing.html.
The pricing page's matrix cells, add-ons, explainer cells, and FAQ items are all intended to be interactive and stateful.
Header navigation items marked with href="#" may be placeholders rather than fully working destinations, so they should be observed for behavior but not assumed to navigate anywhere meaningful.
The lack of console and network errors in prescan suggests functional issues are more likely to be interaction/state or responsive-usability problems than load failures.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html pricing matrix cells: selected-cell state, row/column highlight persistence, and whether all matrix values are selectable including Contact us cells
pricing.html sticky quote card: correct tier/value update after cell clicks and after switching between distant matrix cells
pricing.html 'How we got this number' expander: disclosure behavior, content visibility, and whether it reflects the selected cell
pricing.html add-on checkboxes: combination pricing, percentage vs flat-fee math, and breakdown card updates
pricing.html tier explainer cells: click-to-highlight mapping and whether tier labels remain synchronized with selected matrix region
pricing.html FAQ and feature comparison sections: expand/collapse or row behaviors if present, plus any unexpected layout breakage
index.html and pricing.html top navigation / CTA tap targets: mobile usability risk due to multiple small-tap-target warnings

phases.title: Landing page orientation
phases.objective: Verify the homepage messaging and the paths into pricing from the landing experience.
key_checks: Confirm the hero narrative, SQL example, and three feature cards render coherently.
Click the primary 'See pricing' CTA and confirm it lands on pricing.html.
Check the top navigation links for expected behavior, especially Pricing versus placeholder links like Docs/Customers/Sign in.
exit_criteria: Pricing page is reached from the landing page via the CTA or nav.
No unexpected navigation errors or broken rendering are observed on the landing page.

phases.title: Core pricing matrix validation
phases.objective: Exercise the main two-axis pricing interaction and verify the page responds correctly to different cell selections.
key_checks: Click representative cells across multiple rows and columns, including a low-price cell, a mid-tier cell, a high-price cell, and at least one 'Contact us' cell.
Verify the selected cell state changes, the correct row and column highlight, and the sticky quote card updates to the selected amount and tier.
Confirm the displayed tier labels correspond to the row band and that switching cells clears or updates prior selection state correctly.
exit_criteria: At least one cell from each major row band has been selected.
The quote card and highlighted matrix state have been observed to update consistently across selections.

phases.title: Pricing explanation and add-ons
phases.objective: Validate the supporting pricing logic around the selected cell and the add-on controls that modify monthly cost.
key_checks: Open the 'How we got this number' expansion and confirm the explanatory content appears and remains tied to the selected cell.
Toggle several add-on checkboxes, mixing percentage and flat monthly add-ons, and verify the bottom breakdown card changes appropriately.
Test at least one combination of multiple add-ons to look for stacking, ordering, or total-calculation issues.
exit_criteria: The calculation disclosure has been opened successfully.
Add-on selections visibly affect the breakdown or quote state, and multi-add-on combinations do not break layout or totals.

phases.title: Tier explainer, feature matrix, and FAQ
phases.objective: Check the deeper informational sections for interactive mapping and layout integrity.
key_checks: Click each of the tier explainer cells to confirm the corresponding tier highlight/state changes as expected.
Scan the feature comparison table for readability and any missing alignment or truncation issues.
Interact with the FAQ items if they are expandable, verifying open/close behavior and content completeness.
exit_criteria: The tier mapping interaction has been validated for multiple tiers.
The feature comparison and FAQ sections have been inspected for interaction or layout defects.

phases.title: Responsive/mobile verification
phases.objective: Repeat the most important pricing and navigation interactions in mobile viewport, focusing on tap-target and layout risks.
key_checks: Re-check the header navigation and primary CTA on the landing page for tap usability.
Repeat at least one matrix selection, one add-on toggle, and the calculation expander on pricing.html in mobile viewport.
Look for clipping, overflow, sticky-card obstruction, and any controls that become too small or hard to tap.
exit_criteria: Critical pricing interactions have been confirmed in mobile viewport.
Any tap-target or layout issues are documented with page and control specificity.

coverage_targets.features: exercise the landing CTA, top navigation, pricing matrix, sticky quote card, calculation expander, add-on checkboxes, tier explainer, feature comparison, and FAQ
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat the pricing matrix selection, add-on toggles, and disclosure interaction on a mobile viewport, while checking header/CTA tap targets

notes: Prioritize the matrix and add-on math over placeholder nav links, but still record whether placeholder links are inert or misleading.
Because the prescan already showed multiple small tap targets, mobile checks should explicitly capture any usability regressions rather than treating them as incidental.

findings.user_goal: Compare pricing and choose matrix/add-on options on a phone without fighting the layout
findings.problem: The pricing page overflows the mobile viewport horizontally, so the matrix and lower controls extend beyond the screen and require extra scrolling/panning.
findings.evidence: On mobile, the layout warning reports page width 475px vs 390px viewport, and the observation notes the pricing matrix extends off-screen to the right.
findings.why_it_matters: A pricing page should be easy to scan and compare on mobile; horizontal overflow makes the core matrix harder to read and increases the chance of missed selections.
findings.suggestion: Reflow the matrix into a narrower stacked layout on small screens, or reduce columns/enable a more mobile-friendly comparison pattern so all pricing cells fit within the viewport.

findings.user_goal: Toggle add-ons quickly and accurately on touch devices
findings.problem: The add-on checkboxes are extremely small touch targets, making them difficult to tap reliably on mobile.
findings.evidence: Multiple add-on inputs are 13x13px in the layout warnings, and mobile reflections repeatedly call out the 13x13 checkbox targets as below guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Small checkboxes increase mis-taps and frustration, especially when users are trying to build a final monthly quote from several add-ons.
findings.suggestion: Increase the hit area around each checkbox and label to at least mobile guidance, ideally by making the entire row clickable and adding more vertical spacing.

findings.user_goal: Understand how the quoted price is calculated
findings.problem: The 'How we got this number' / 'Overview' disclosure appears to do nothing when tapped, so users do not get visible calculation details.
findings.evidence: Clicking Overview only changed the URL fragment to # with no visible expansion on desktop and mobile; the recent trajectory says the disclosure did not visibly expand and explanation content remained hidden.
findings.why_it_matters: Pricing transparency depends on users being able to inspect how the total is built. A dead or ambiguous disclosure undermines confidence in the estimate.
findings.suggestion: Make the disclosure open with a clear animation/state change and ensure the expanded explanation is visible and scannable immediately below the selected quote.

findings.user_goal: Use navigation links and expect real destinations
findings.problem: Several prominent links behave like placeholders or dead ends rather than real navigation, including Book demo, Docs, About, Architecture, Customers, and some footer items.
findings.evidence: Book demo stayed on the same URL with no visible change on mobile and desktop; Docs and Customers only appended #; About and Architecture also produced no visible page change.
findings.why_it_matters: When obvious CTAs and navigation items go nowhere, users may question whether the site is complete or trustworthy, especially on a marketing/pricing page.
findings.suggestion: Replace placeholder hashes with real destinations, or disable/label unfinished links clearly so users do not think they missed a page load.

findings.user_goal: Move from pricing to a meaningful booking action
findings.problem: The Book demo control looks prominent but does not provide a booking flow or even clear feedback after activation.
findings.evidence: On mobile, Book demo remained on the same pricing URL after tap with no visible-text or navigation change; desktop testing also found it only changed the URL to pricing.html#.
findings.why_it_matters: A primary CTA that appears important but goes nowhere creates a dead-end at the moment of intent, which can cost conversions and erode confidence.
findings.suggestion: Route Book demo to a real booking/contact flow or convert it to a clearly labeled placeholder if it is not ready.

findings.user_goal: Use the pricing page comfortably on touch screens
findings.problem: Top navigation links are also below mobile tap-size guidance, so the header is harder to use precisely on small screens.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag small tap targets such as Lattice DB 123x28, Pricing 45x21, and Book demo 105x41; trajectory notes also mention several header links below the 44px mobile guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Tiny header targets make it easy to mis-tap navigation and increase friction when users try to move between pricing and the rest of the site on mobile.
findings.suggestion: Increase header link padding, add more spacing between items, and ensure the brand/CTA are comfortably tappable on phones.

findings.user_goal: Interpret which pricing tier a selected matrix cell belongs to
findings.problem: The pricing page’s tier explainer is present, but the interaction model is not very discoverable on mobile because the selected cell and explanation are separated by a long, dense scroll.
findings.evidence: The final observation shows the selected cell and quote near the middle of a tall page, with the tier explainer, feature matrix, and FAQ much farther below; prior chunks note scrolling is needed to reach the lower explanation sections.
findings.why_it_matters: When explanation content is far away from the pricing selection, users may not connect the tier label to the matrix choice or may stop before finding the supporting details.
findings.suggestion: Bring the tier explanation closer to the selected quote on mobile, or add a compact inline summary that explains the selected tier without requiring a long scroll.

gaps: Only directly exercised 37% of visible interactive feature signatures.
